samples.question: The picture shows four counters standing side by side. Each counter is a column of four square cells and a coloured bar at the top; the four top bars are red, blue, green and orange, and the top bar is that counter's colour. A counter's reading is how many of its cells are shaded dark; cells shade from the bottom upwards, so a counter reads 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4. The columns as drawn show every counter's starting reading. Below the counters is a row of white cards, and the grey arrow says to apply them one at a time from left to right. Each card carries a coloured square naming the counter it acts on, which is the counter whose top bar has that same colour, and one, two or three black dots giving how many steps that card applies to that counter. One step works like this: if the named counter is not already full, one more of its cells becomes shaded, so its reading goes up by one; but if the named counter is already full, that is, all four of its cells are shaded, then instead every one of its cells is cleared so it reads 0 and one single step is passed to the counter immediately to its left, and that step then follows this very same rule on that neighbour, which may in turn clear and pass a step further left. A step passed leftwards out of the leftmost counter is simply discarded. Counters keep their colour and their place throughout, and a card affects only the counter it names and any counters reached by passed steps. The magenta ring below the counters marks the queried counter. After all the cards have been applied in order, what is the reading of the queried counter, that is, how many of its cells are shaded? Answer with one of: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
